name: Hindulotine
description: Hindulotine control is the rubber-guard Hindu configuration in which the bottom player loops an arm over the raised foot and around the opponent's shoulder to set a leg-in guillotine.
variant_uniqueness: Hindu control for a leg-in guillotine
summary: Hindulotine control is the rubber-guard Hindu configuration in which the bottom player loops an arm over the raised foot and around the opponent's shoulder to set a leg-in guillotine.
overview:
The bottom player is on the back or hip with the raised rubber-guard knee close to the torso. The controlling arm passes over the foot and around the opponent's shoulder into the head-control space. The leg remains part of the enclosure when the hands connect for the choke. The top player faces the guard player and must address the neck enclosure even if the lower leg is passed.

Hindu Control is the holding configuration; Hindulotine names the choke applied from it. The raised leg contributes to head control, so an ordinary front-headlock guillotine does not by itself establish this position. Terminology: Hindu Control.

Hug the knee and turn onto the hip to create room for the arm path. Bring the elbow above the raised foot and the hand around the shoulder rather than forcing it straight through a closed gap. Hold the head and leg enclosure without finishing pressure before seeking the second hand.

A choke can impair consciousness quickly. Drill the entry without neck pressure, never add a neck twist, and release both hands and the high leg on any tap or loss of normal responsiveness.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — Hindu Control to Hindulotine](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y5ZQNgG2hNc); [Ben Eddy — later Hindulotine S-grip clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/printthread.php?page=2&pp=10&t=22650).
key_principles: Keep the knee supported: Hug the knee and turn onto the hip to create room for the arm path.
Loop around the foot: Bring the elbow above the raised foot and the hand around the shoulder rather than forcing it straight through a closed gap.
Establish Hindu Control: Hold the head and leg enclosure without finishing pressure before seeking the second hand.
Connect a controlled grip: Use the grip taught by your instructor; Ben Eddy's later S-grip teaching differs from his early reverse-gable demonstration.
Treat a pass as a new check: Do not assume the choke has disappeared merely because the opponent clears the lower leg.
Release the entire enclosure: Open the hands and move the controlling leg away immediately when a partner taps or stops responding normally.

top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The bottom player is on the back or hip with the raised rubber-guard knee close to the torso. The controlling arm passes over the foot and around the opponent's shoulder into the head-control space. The leg remains part of the enclosure when the hands connect for the choke. The top player faces the guard player and must address the neck enclosure even if the lower leg is passed.

An elbow traveling over the opponent's raised foot toward your shoulder signals Hindu Control. Avoid twisting the head against a fixed leg-and-arm enclosure. Use an inside hand frame before the attacker connects the finishing grip.

Clearing the lower leg alone may leave the neck caught; address the upper enclosure first. Move the head and shoulders free after the hand and high-leg controls have loosened. Do not wait for dizziness or severe pain before stopping a choke attempt.

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: which arm movement signals the developing Hindu Control enclosure?
flashcards.answer: An elbow traveling over the opponent's raised foot toward your shoulder signals Hindu Control.
flashcards.answer_line: Their elbow passes over the raised foot toward your shoulder

plausible: Their elbow remains below the raised foot as the hand reaches up
Their hand stays outside your shoulder instead of circling toward the head
trap: Their forearm stays across your waist below the high leg

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: what makes turning your head against the closed enclosure hazardous?
flashcards.answer: Avoid twisting the head against a fixed leg-and-arm enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: The arm and leg can hold the neck while the body rotates

plausible: The foot follows the head before the connected arms move
Turning the jaw past the forearm opens the hand connection
trap: The knee hug diverts the turning force into the chest

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: before the finishing hands join, where should your frame work?
flashcards.answer: Use an inside hand frame before the attacker connects the finishing grip.

plausible: Outside their wrists while the hands remain free to meet
On the raised foot alone while the hand-joining route stays open
trap: On the mat behind you before interrupting the supporting hand

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: why doesn't clearing the lower leg prove the choke has opened?
flashcards.answer: The lower-body pass can leave the hands and raised leg enclosing the neck. Check that connection rather than treating a new hip position as a release.
flashcards.answer_line: The upper arm-and-leg connection can remain around the neck

plausible: The low hook was the only connection keeping the hands joined
Moving beside the ribs stops the high foot reaching the head
trap: The new side position forces the supporting hand to separate

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: what must loosen before you withdraw your head and raise your shoulders?
flashcards.answer: Move the head and shoulders free after the hand and high-leg controls have loosened.
flashcards.answer_line: The hand grip and the high-leg control

plausible: Only the low leg crossing while the upper enclosure stays closed
Only one wrist while the other arm and raised foot retain the head
trap: Only the hip angle without changing the hand-and-foot enclosure

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: why should a secured choke be stopped before dizziness?
flashcards.answer: Do not wait for dizziness or severe pain before stopping a choke attempt.

plausible: Normal breathing proves that the secured loop cannot affect circulation
Passing the hips prevents the joined hands from compressing the neck
trap: A free hand proves you can pull the head out after symptoms begin

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: where is the attacker's raised knee as the arm circles toward you?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player is on the back or hip with the raised rubber-guard knee close to the torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Close to their torso in high guard

plausible: Flat between your knees on the mat
Extended away behind your shoulder
trap: Locked straight against your lower back

flashcards.question: Hindulotine defense: what separates this enclosure from an ordinary front-headlock guillotine?
flashcards.answer: Hindu Control is the holding configuration; Hindulotine names the choke applied from it. The raised leg contributes to head control, so an ordinary front-headlock guillotine does not by itself establish this position.
flashcards.answer_line: A raised guard leg participates in controlling the head

plausible: A neck loop formed only by the arms with no raised foot involved
A high supporting elbow over the shoulder without a leg in the loop
trap: An opposing arm included beside the neck within an arm-only enclosure

flashcards.question: Hindu Control: how do you make room for the arm while supporting the raised knee?
flashcards.answer: Hug the knee and turn onto the hip to create room for the arm path.
flashcards.answer_line: Hug the knee and turn onto your hip

plausible: Pull the ankle sideways with the knee fixed
Flatten both hips and extend the raised leg
trap: Let the knee fall away while reaching overhead

flashcards.question: Hindu Control: which route does your controlling arm take?
flashcards.answer: Bring the elbow above the raised foot and the hand around the shoulder rather than forcing it straight through a closed gap.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow over the foot, hand around the shoulder

plausible: Elbow below the raised foot while the hand reaches for the shoulder
Hand forced through the closed foot-to-head gap without clearing the elbow
trap: Elbow outside the high leg with the forearm still across the waist

flashcards.question: Hindu Control: before reaching for the second hand, what should already be stable?
flashcards.answer: Hold the head and leg enclosure without finishing pressure before seeking the second hand.
flashcards.answer_line: The head held within the arm-and-leg enclosure

plausible: A high shin near the head with the elbow still below the foot
Both hands pulling while the high leg stays loose
trap: The head contact alone after the knee hug has been released

flashcards.question: Hindulotine: how do Ben Eddy's early and later demonstrations differ in their hand connection?
flashcards.answer: Use the grip taught by your instructor; Ben Eddy's later S-grip teaching differs from his early reverse-gable demonstration.

plausible: First finger hooks, then palms joined without hooking fingers
The same reverse-gable connection in both lessons
trap: Early double-wrist connection; later plain palm-to-palm grip

flashcards.question: Hindu Control: which connection decides whether the neck stays restrained after the lower-leg pass?
flashcards.answer: Check the retained high leg-and-arm connection. A lower-body pass can occur while this upper enclosure remains closed.
flashcards.answer_line: The upper enclosure around the head

plausible: The low ankle crossing that the opponent has already passed
The location of the lower foot on the mat by itself
trap: The passing knee moving beyond the hip without checking the hands

flashcards.question: Hindulotine: what must you release when your partner taps?
flashcards.answer: Open the hands and move the controlling leg away immediately when a partner taps or stops responding normally.
flashcards.answer_line: Separate the hands and move the controlling leg away

plausible: Open one hand while keeping the leg clamped
Relax your fingers but keep pulling with the elbow
trap: Move the low leg while leaving the head enclosure closed

flashcards.question: Hindu Control: where should your raised knee stay relative to your trunk?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player is on the back or hip with the raised rubber-guard knee close to the torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Close enough to support beside the torso

plausible: Fully straight above the opponent's head
Resting flat beneath the opponent's hip
trap: Spread wide while the ankle is pulled inward

flashcards.question: Hindu Control: what changes when the holding configuration becomes a Hindulotine attempt?
flashcards.answer: Hindu Control is the holding configuration; Hindulotine names the choke applied from it. The raised leg contributes to head control, so an ordinary front-headlock guillotine does not by itself establish this position.
flashcards.answer_line: The connected enclosure applies choking pressure

plausible: The hands separate while the high leg remains in place
The lower leg changes position without loading the neck enclosure
trap: The knee loses support while the foot is pulled away from the torso
